ky_global_village.blurb: Global Village is a sandstone cliff in the Natural Bridge Region of the Red River Gorge, set well back from the pavement in Daniel Boone National Forest. It holds a bit over twenty climbs split nearly evenly between bolted lines and traditional routes. Grades run from easy 5.6 and 5.7 outings up through the low 5.13s, with a good cluster of moderate leads on the left side and the steeper, harder sport climbing toward the right end. Once a quiet spot for hard locals, it became busy after beginner-friendly routes were added. Expect a muddy, steep, wooded hike of roughly twenty minutes, so it suits those who don't mind a real walk.

ky_sanitarium.blurb: Sanitarium is a tall, orange, steeply angled wall within the Miller Fork preserve in the Red River Gorge, tucked between the Nursery and Vine Wall. Nearly everything here is bolted, with a lone trad line, and the grades span from the easy end of 5.6 through the 5.12s, with the bulk of the lines in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Climbs are roughly 90 feet at the long end and tend to include roofs and traverses before an overhung finish. The wall catches morning light, sees fairly little traffic, and some lines are sandy or in need of brushing. Watch for poison ivy along the base, especially on the left.

ky_south_park.blurb: South Park is a newer, still-growing sport crag in the Bald Rock Fork preserve of the Red River Gorge. Around two dozen routes, almost all bolted, hang on a big amphitheater with a main cave and a shorter wall to the left that collects the moderates. Grades start at about 5.6, then stack up heavily in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a few lines in the low 5.13s. The rock is sharp and grippy but can be loose, with small nubs breaking off, so helmets and care matter. The setting is shady and secluded, and visitors report having the place to themselves. Some of the newest lines are not rain-protected.

ky_wall_of_denial.blurb: Wall of Denial is a remote cliff in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, reached by a long, easy-to-misjudge hike through rhododendron. It faces south and is mainly a traditional crag, with most of its twenty-odd routes needing a rack and only a few bolted lines. Grades go from easy 5.6 and 5.7 climbs through a solid group of 5.9s and into the 5.11s, topping out around 5.12. Because of the walk it tends to feel quieter and more adventurous than the roadside walls, and the effort is generally considered worth it for the varied, good-quality lines.

ky_phantasia.blurb: Phantasia is a roadside crag in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, just past the Iron Bridge and said to be the area's first roadside sport wall. About twenty routes are split between trad and sport, with some top-rope options, and the grade range is unusually wide: a few easy 5.5 to 5.7 lines, a middle group of 5.8 to 5.10, and several steep testpieces into the 5.12s and one low 5.13. The wall faces mostly northeast and the rock quality is good. Its steep roofs and slabs make it a handy stop for a mixed group, with a short walk from the pullout.

ky_deep_end.blurb: Deep End is a shady, overhanging section of the Miller Fork preserve in the Red River Gorge. The twenty-odd lines are mostly bolted, with a handful of trad climbs and one boulder problem, and are generally pocketed and steep. Grades run from easy 5.8 into the 5.13s, with the best concentration from 5.10 up, and the central cave holds the hardest sport lines. The routes reach roughly 60 to 85 feet. Because it stays mostly out of the sun and is steep enough to keep dry, it is considered a good choice for summer days. From the parking lot, the approach is a stroll along an old road, then a short, rutted hill.
